html:
French Indochina was the union of French colonies and protectorates in mainland Southeast Asia, from 1887 to 1954. The map shows it from 1880 to 1914, the years it was put together.

France built it piece by piece:

  • Cochinchina, the south of Vietnam, taken as a colony between 1858 and 1867;
  • Cambodia, a protectorate from 1863;
  • Annam and Tonkin, central and northern Vietnam, after the Sino French War of 1884 and 1885;
  • Laos, added in the 1890s.

The union was formed in 1887, with a governor general who later sat in Hanoi. Paul Doumer, governor general from 1897 to 1902, paid for railways (North to South railway) and bridges with state monopolies on opium, salt and alcohol, which fell hard on peasants. The colony exported rice and later rubber.

Vietnamese resistance never stopped. A royalist revolt lasted into the 1890s, and new nationalists studied abroad. Hồ Chí Minh was born in Annam in 1890. The interwar years are under French Indo-China.
